title: Finding Sita
hook: the garden; the ring; "I'm not leaving without you"

segments.voice: Yesterday, the leap: a mountain turned down, and a thumb-sized escape from Surasa's mouth. Your line was the leap is the practice. Did you take a first step? Today, Hanuman lands. Day thirty-three.

Lanka at night. A city of gold, full of music and feasting and guards. Hanuman shrinks to the size of a cat and searches. Palace after palace. Room after room. He sees the demon king Ravana's wives asleep, and for a moment he thinks one of them might be Sita, and then stops himself: no. Sita would never be sleeping peacefully here. He almost gives up. Then, at the edge of the city, he finds a garden, a grove of ashoka trees. And under one tree, guarded by fierce women, sits a woman in a single worn cloth, thin from grief, refusing everything she's offered. He climbs into the branches above her and waits.
screen: `A CITY OF GOLD, AT NIGHT.` → `NOT HER. NOT HERE.` → `A GARDEN OF ASHOKA TREES.` → `A WOMAN UNDER A TREE.`

segments.voice: Hanuman has a problem. If a giant monkey drops out of a tree in the enemy's city and says, hi, Rama sent me, she'll scream, and he'll be caught. So he does something gentle. Hidden in the leaves, he begins quietly telling Rama's story, the story she knows best, in a soft voice. Sita looks up. Then he comes down, bows, and gives her the one thing that proves who he is: Rama's ring. She holds it and weeps, the text says, as if she were holding Rama himself. And then Hanuman makes an offer. Climb on my back. I'll carry you across the ocean tonight. You'll be with Rama by morning. Many people remember this moment as Hanuman saying: I'm not leaving without you. That's the feeling of the scene. But in Valmiki, the one who says no is Sita. She won't go. She gives two reasons. She won't willingly touch any man but her husband. And she wants Rama to come himself, and end this properly. Then she takes a jewel from her hair and gives it to Hanuman, and tells him a small private story only Rama would know, so Rama will believe him. Ring in, jewel out. Here's what the story knows. Hanuman crossed an ocean, and the most important thing he carried was tiny: a ring. Proof that she wasn't forgotten. In a city full of people telling her to give up, that ring said someone is coming. Bring the ring. Whoever is waiting for you needs proof you remember.
screen: `HE TELLS RAMA'S STORY, SOFTLY.` · `THE RING.` · `CLIMB ON MY BACK. SHE SAYS NO.` · `RING IN, JEWEL OUT.` · then, large: `BRING THE RING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: a promise you keep quietly. Sit and breathe. Think of someone who is waiting on you. Maybe they don't even say so. A parent who waits for a call. A friend going through something. A child. What's the ring you could bring them: small, real proof that you haven't forgotten? Hold that person in mind for the whole sit. If you pray, you can hold them before God. The bell holds the time.
Finding Sita. Hanuman finds her in the ashoka grove, gives her Rama's ring, and carries back her hair jewel as proof.
Your line: bring the ring. Today, send one small proof to someone who is waiting: a message, a call, a visit. Day thirty-three.

howItsDone: The scene of Hanuman giving Rama's ring to Sita in the ashoka grove is one of the most painted and performed in the Ramayana, and it's a high point when devotees recite the Sundara Kanda.

trapdoor: what you thought: the monkey rescues the princess.
what it means: Hanuman brings a ring, proof she isn't forgotten, and Sita chooses to wait for Rama.
what a scholar hears: in Valmiki, Sita herself refuses rescue by Hanuman and sends her chudamani and a private memory as tokens; the rescue is left to Rama.

notes: The outline's hook line "I'm not leaving without you" is not in Valmiki; the script presents it as how people remember the scene and gives Valmiki's actual scene, in which Sita declines. A Keeper may prefer to revise the index hook.
Sita's reasons (not willingly touching another man; wanting Rama to win her back) follow Sundara Kanda ~37; confirm.
The private story is the crow incident (Sundara Kanda 38); left unnamed. Confirm.
Hanuman's size in the search ('size of a cat') follows common tellings; confirm.
